title: NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS)
sources: Brott T, Adams HP Jr, Olinger CP, et al. Measurements of acute cerebral infarction: a clinical examination scale. Stroke. 1989;20(7):864-870
NIH Stroke Scale, National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) — training, certification, and scoring materials

Adams HP Jr, Davis PH, Leira EC, et al. Baseline NIH Stroke Scale score strongly predicts outcome after stroke: a report of the TOAST trial. Neurology. 1999;53(1):126-131 (score-to-outcome relationship)

changelog.change: Expanded sources with the full Brott 1989 citation, the NINDS scale materials, and Adams 1999 (TOAST) for the score-to-outcome relationship; named the severity-band scheme and its alternate in notes; removed the needs-primary-source flag.
Item score ranges only, per the deliberate scope decision in Calculator_Logic_Build_Spec.md.

purpose: Standardized stroke severity — drives thrombolytic/thrombectomy eligibility and serial monitoring. Enter the item scores a trained examiner has already determined.
notes: Per the build spec's deliberate scope decision, the per-point behavioral criteria (what separates a 1 from a 2 on each item) are NOT encoded here — that is certified-examiner territory. This tool sums the item scores you enter. Severity bands shown (0 none / 1-4 minor / 5-15 moderate / 16-20 moderate-severe / 21-42 severe) follow the NINDS NIH Stroke Scale descriptors used in the scale's training materials; an alternate common scheme is < 5 / 5-14 / 15-24 / > 24. Bands are for communication and trending — thrombolytic and thrombectomy decisions use the specific trial criteria and clinical context, not a cut-point. Higher baseline score predicts worse outcome (Adams 1999): roughly ≤ 6 favours a good outcome and ≥ 16 a high probability of death or severe disability.
buildNote: Severity cut-points vary by source (build spec notes an alternate <5 / 5-14 / 15-24 scheme). One stratification is used here; cite it in the UI. All 15 items must be entered for the total to display.
